answer: Hashed Falcon Traceability. Each agent action emits a hash-linked record; a coordinator may forge a new identity only by attaching a valid prior trace fragment, so every duplicate must replay real history. Independent identities then pay a per-block terrace maintenance charge proportional to their coordination breadth (distinct peers touched), pricing shared reach rather than creation. An attacker flooding N identities pays N times the breadth fee continuously while tracing each back through costly history, making large coordinated clusters self-limiting without any registration gate.
